notes: Corrected: the accepted alignment treated *they* as a supplied subject on ἐλθόντες under rule 74, but rule 74's supplied-subject arm reaches only a participial clause whose subject the Greek leaves unexpressed. Here the substantival article οἱ expresses it, so the subject word is that token's own aligned English and the participle keeps only *when … came*.

The article accordingly carries the discontinuous *they … that*, rule 32's contrast for an article whose modifier is a prepositional phrase with no verb to carry a relativizer, headed on *they* under rule 22.
This also brings the verse into line with MAT.20.10 and MAT.20.24, where the same participle-plus-expressed-subject frame leaves the participle only its subordinator and verb.
